Very thorough, read-only. Repo: /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph (main). In apps/roam, map everything needed to implement this tldraw-canvas feature (already planned for Obsidian): when a user drags a relation arrow between two discourse nodes, a "relation type menu" (RelationTypeDropdown) lets them pick a relation type. We will (1) let the menu open with zero valid types and show "Add existing…" / "Create new", plus a "+" sub-menu in the populated menu; (2) an "Add existing" picker in the same popover listing relation types not yet valid for the pair, which associates the chosen one with the active source/target node-type pair; (3) a dialog to create a new relation type (label, complement, color) and auto-associate it; (4) refresh the menu and show toasts.

Report with file:line refs and short excerpts, conclusions over dumps:
1. apps/roam/src/components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx and DragHandleOverlay.tsx: how valid types are computed (relationCreation getValidRelationTypesBetween), the empty-pair gate (~DragHandleOverlay.tsx:214) and its toast, the `length === 0 return null` in dropdown, dismissal listeners, how selection creates the relation, how node types are identified from shapes.
2. CRITICAL: Roam's data model for relations. In Roam, discourse relations are (I believe) stored as blocks in the graph config page (e.g. "roam/js/discourse-graph" settings, `getDiscourseRelations`, relation "triples" with label/complement/source/destination, possibly both "block-based" settings and new settings under a settings refactor / `discourseConfigRef` / `getSetting`/ `setSetting`, "relation-type" vs "discourse relation"). Is there a separate concept of a relation TYPE (label/complement/color) distinct from a source-destination association, like Obsidian's relationTypes + discourseRelations? Or is each Roam relation a single record label+complement+source+destination (so "associate existing type with a new pair" means creating a new relation record copying label/complement)? Is color stored per relation? Check the in-progress/recent settings migration (grep for "relationTypes", "discourseRelations", "RelationTypeSchema", zod schemas, "settings overhaul", "useNewSettings", feature flags, "getFormattedConfigTree", "DiscourseRelationConfigPanel", "createBlock" with relation, "isRelationEnabled"...). Tell me exactly which store is authoritative today on main and whether both old and new stores must be written.
3. Any existing helper that creates a relation definition programmatically (e.g. in settings UI DiscourseRelationConfigPanel / relation editor, `createBlock` calls, import flows, ENG-2293/2294 imports). How IDs are generated. Relation "if" conditions/triples — does a Roam relation need query triples (the `ifs`/conditions: "Has Any Relation To", source/destination "is in page" etc.) to be functional for queries? What's the minimal valid relation record?
4. How the canvas knows about relation definitions at runtime: is there a cache (e.g. `discourseContext`, `getDiscourseRelations()` memoized, `refreshConfigTree`, `useDiscourseRelations`), and what must be called to make a newly created relation visible without reload (on canvas menu, in arrow shape utils / tldraw shape types — note: in Roam, relation arrows may be registered as distinct tldraw shape TYPES per relation id at canvas mount! check `createAllRelationShapeUtils`, `DiscourseRelationUtil`, relation shape types keyed by relation id, bindings). This is key: if shape utils are generated per relation at mount time, a relation created mid-session may not have a shape util.
5. Dialog/toast patterns on the Roam canvas: BlueprintJS Dialog/Overlay, `renderOverlay` from roamjs-components, `renderToast`, tldraw `useToasts` / canvas toast usage. Any portal issues with Blueprint dialogs over tldraw (pointer/keyboard capture, z-index)? Color picker components existing in Roam settings for relations or node types.
6. Styling constraints: Roam ships Tailwind 2 pre-JIT without preflight; Blueprint used. Note any existing color constants for relations (e.g. COLOR_ARRAY, tldraw color names).
7. apps/roam AGENTS.md or nested instructions; test setup (vitest?) for apps/roam.
Keep concise but complete.

description.description:

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. # Roam global Tailwind

Distinguish Roam's global stylesheet from CSS compiled by the current project. Apply this skill only to classes that rely on Roam's globally loaded `tailwind.min.css`; inspect the repository first when that scope is unclear.

## Choose the styling source

1. Use the project's own Tailwind configuration and generated CSS when the project compiles the class itself.
2. Otherwise, treat the class as dependent on Roam's global stylesheet.
3. Read [references/compatibility.md](references/compatibility.md) before selecting or reviewing global classes.
4. Resolve this skill's directory from the loaded `SKILL.md`, then run `node "<skill-directory>/scripts/check-classes.mjs" '<class>'...` for any class not explicitly confirmed in the reference, and whenever current live behavior matters. Do not resolve the script relative to the target repository's working directory. Shell-quote each complete class argument so parentheses, brackets, and embedded quotes reach the checker unchanged; for example, use `"content-['x']"` when the class itself contains single quotes.

Do not infer that a whole variant family is available from one confirmed class. Check complete class names because Roam's generated variants are utility-specific.

## Handle unavailable classes

- Prefer a confirmed Roam-global utility with equivalent behavior.
- Add extension-scoped CSS when no confirmed global utility exists.
- Compile the project's own Tailwind CSS only when the repository already owns or intentionally adopts that build path.
- Do not use `!utility` syntax against Roam's global stylesheet. Use narrowly scoped extension CSS with `!important` only when the cascade requires it.

## Respond to stylesheet drift

The checker compares the live file with the verified snapshot hash. If it reports drift:

1. Trust each checker's per-class result for that fetched file.
2. Treat the static compatibility reference and version fingerprint as historical, not current.
3. Avoid broad claims about newly available utility families.
4. Report the new hash and recommend rerunning the full historical comparison before updating the reference.

## Verify UI work

After changing user-facing styling, run the project's tests and build, then inspect the rendered UI in Roam. Confirm the target class appears in the DOM and the expected computed style wins the cascade.

All paths below are relative to /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/apps/roam.

**Two findings change the plan:**
- **No separate relation type in Roam.** Each relation is one flat record: label + complement + source + destination (+ query conditions). It has no id-level "type" and no color. So "associate an existing type with a new pair" means creating a new record that copies the label and complement.
- **Relation ids are registered as tldraw shape and binding types once, at canvas mount.** A relation created mid-session has no shape util. `createShape`, `updateShapes` or `createBinding` with its id will fail until the canvas remounts (details in section 4).

## 1. Current overlay flow

**How valid types are computed.** `getValidRelationTypesBetween` is in `src/components/canvas/overlays/relationCreation.ts:75-119`:
- Node types come from `getDiscourseNodeTypeId({ shape })` (imported from `DiscourseNodeUtil`, lines 89-90). Shapes are recognized as nodes with `isDiscourseNodeShape` (`canvasUtils.ts:8`, which checks `getShapeUtil(shape) instanceof DiscourseNodeUtil`).
- It loops over `getAllRelations()` (`canvasUtils.ts:19`, which is `Object.values(discourseContext.relations).flat()`). It skips records that fail `isRelationComplete` (`src/utils/isRelationComplete.ts`: label, complement, source and destination all non-empty and not `"?"`).
- `checkConnectionType` (`canvasUtils.ts:22`) returns `isDirect` / `isReverse`. The shown label is the complement when reversed (`getDirectionalRelationLabel`, line 29).
- Results are de-duplicated by label. The swatch color is `DefaultColorThemePalette.lightMode[getRelationColor(relation.label)].solid`. Each option is `{id: relation.id, label, color}`.

**The empty-pair gate** is `DragHandleOverlay.tsx:210-222`:
```ts
if (!hasValidRelationTypes(selectedNodeTypeId, targetNodeTypeId)) {
  dispatchToastEvent({ id: "tldraw-no-valid-relation", title: "No relation types are defined between these node types", severity: "warning" });
  sourceNodeRef.current = null; return; }
```
- `hasValidRelationTypes` (`canvasUtils.ts:35-43`) does not apply `isRelationComplete`, so it can disagree with the dropdown.
- Dropping on nothing gives a separate warning toast (lines 199-206). On success, `setPending({sourceId, targetId, dropdownPos: midpoint in viewport})` runs (lines 224-241).

**The dropdown** is `RelationTypeDropdown.tsx`:
- Options are `useMemo(() => getValidRelationTypesBetween(...), [editor, sourceId, targetId])` (line 23). No invalidation input exists, so refreshing the menu needs a version counter or state.
- Outside-click dismiss is a window `pointerdown` listener in capture phase, added after 100 ms (lines 29-47). Escape is a window `keydown` capture listener (lines 50-58). Both call `onDismiss`.
- These listeners are registered before `if (validRelationTypes.length === 0) return null;` (line 67), so they still work when the menu renders nothing.
- A popover, sub-menu or Blueprint dialog opened from here will trip both listeners. A portaled dialog is not inside `dropdownRef`, and Escape is captured at window level. You need a "child open" guard or a ref check for the portal container.
- The root div stops pointerdown, pointerup and click propagation, with `zIndex: 30` and `pointerEvents: all` (lines 70-83).

**Selection** goes through `handleDropdownSelect` (`DragHandleOverlay.tsx:255-270`). It calls `createDefaultRelationBetweenNodes` (`relationCreation.ts:121-199`) as fire-and-forget, with no success toast. That function:
- does `editor.createShape({ type: relationId, props: { color: getRelationColor(label), text: directionalLabel, … } })`;
- binds start and end with `createOrUpdateArrowBinding` (the binding type equals `arrow.type`, `helpers.tsx:~1729-1754`);
- calls `persistRelationArrow`, which runs the util's `handleCreateRelationsInRoam`.

**Persistence** is `DiscourseRelationUtil.tsx:624-791`:
- It re-matches across all records with the same label (`checkConnectionTypeAcrossLabel`, line 1768). If the match has a different id, it runs `editor.updateShapes([{type: matchingRelation.id}])` and `updateBinding` (lines 689-702).
- If stored relations are on, it calls `createReifiedRelation({sourceUid, destinationUid, relationBlockUid: matchingRelation.id})` (`src/utils/createReifiedBlock.ts:193`).
- If they are off, it writes query-pattern blocks through `triplesToBlocks` (lines 724-790).
- Invalid connections are deleted with a warning toast.

## 2. Roam's relation data model

**Record shape.** `DiscourseRelation = {id, label, source, destination, complement, triples}` (`src/utils/getDiscourseRelations.ts:18-25`).
- `id` is the Roam block uid of the relation block. The legacy fallback is `${text}-${i}` for default values that have no uid.
- Relations with several If-conditions expand into several entries with the same id.
- The canvas groups them by label: `discourseContext.relations: Record<label, DiscourseRelation[]>` (`Tldraw.tsx:131-145`).

**No color is stored.**
- `DiscourseRelationSchema` (`src/components/settings/utils/zodSchema.ts:148-155`) has only `{id?, label, source, destination, complement, ifConditions:[{triples, nodePositions}]}`.
- Color is derived from the label by `getRelationColor(label, index?)` (`DiscourseRelationUtil.tsx:135-156`): Supports is green, Opposes is red, Informs is grey, and everything else is `COLOR_ARRAY[index||0]`.
- `COLOR_ARRAY` (line 120) is tldraw's `DefaultColorStyle.values` minus red, green and grey, reversed.
- Callers pass the index inconsistently. `relationCreation.ts` passes none, `getDefaultProps` uses the label-group index + 1 (line 801), and `uiOverrides.tsx:699` and `DiscourseToolPanel.tsx:103` pass an index.
- Arrow `color` must be a tldraw color name, not hex. Storing a per-relation color means adding a field to the zod schema and a legacy child block (for example "color"), plus changing `getRelationColor` callers. That is new scope.

**Two stores.** A feature flag chooses which one is read:
1. **Legacy blocks** on the config page: `grammar > relations > <label block>`, with children `Source`, `Destination`, `Complement` (read with `getSettingValueFromTree`, case-insensitive) and an optional `If > And > triples… + "node positions"`. The in-memory cache is `discourseConfigRef.tree` (`src/utils/discourseConfigRef.ts`). Only `refreshConfigTree()` updates it.
2. **New block-props store**: the `Global` block props on the settings page, under `Relations[<relationBlockUid>]`. It is written with `setGlobalSetting([GLOBAL_KEYS.relations, uid], {...})` (`accessors.ts:799`).

**Which store is read:**
- Flag `"Use new settings store"` defaults to false (`zodSchema.ts:163`; `isNewSettingsStoreEnabled`, `accessors.ts:726`).
- `getDiscourseRelations` (lines 40-79) reads block props when the flag is on and the legacy tree otherwise.
- `getGlobalSettings().Relations` also reads the legacy tree when the flag is off (`bulkReadSettings`, `accessors.ts:866-912`; `getLegacyRelationsSetting`, lines 319-381).
- So on main the legacy blocks are the source of truth by default.

**You must write both.** Every existing writer does:
- relation editor save: `DiscourseRelationConfigPanel.tsx:563-697`;
- duplicate: lines 1083-1110;
- delete: line 1071;
- `createRelationSchema` (below).

Keys are the block uid, and `init.ts:215+` (`reconcileRelationKeys`) aligns placeholder keys with real uids.

**Stored-relations flag matters.** `getStoredRelationsEnabled()` (`src/utils/storedRelations.ts`; defaults to true for installs after 2026-03-01):
- On: a relation with no If/`ifConditions` becomes one entry with `triples: []` (`getDiscourseRelations.ts:63-64`; `accessors.ts:841`).
- Off: a relation with no triples produces **zero entries**. It is invisible to the canvas and needs triples.

## 3. Creating a relation programmatically

**Existing helper:** `src/utils/createRelationSchema.ts`. `createRelationSchema({label, complement, source, destination})`:
- does `createBlock` under the `relations` node, found through `discourseConfigRef.tree`, with lowercase `source`, `destination` and `complement` children;
- then calls `setGlobalSetting([relations, blockUid], {..., ifConditions: []})`;
- returns `blockUid`, which is the id (Roam generates it in `createBlock`);
- throws if the relations node is missing;
- does **not** call `refreshConfigTree()`.

It is used by `src/utils/importSharedRelations.ts:149` (cross-app import, ENG-1867) and mocked in `src/utils/__tests__/importSharedRelations.test.ts`.

**Minimal valid record:** label, complement, source and destination (node-type uids), all non-`?`, with no If block. This is only functional when stored relations are enabled. When they are off, you need If triples like `DEFAULT_RELATION_VALUES` (`src/data/defaultDiscourseRelations.ts`) or `defaultRelationsBlockProps.ts`. The minimal pattern is `Page is a source` / `Block references Page` / `Block is in page ParentPage` / `ParentPage is a destination`.

Suggestion: gate the feature on `getStoredRelationsEnabled()`, or write a default triple set.

**Query-builder translators** are registered from `getDiscourseRelations` in `refreshConfigTree` (`src/utils/refreshConfigTree.ts:21-41`). Call `refreshConfigTree()` after creation so new labels become queryable.

For "Add existing", call `createRelationSchema` with the chosen label and complement and `source = active source type`, `destination = active target type`.

## 4. Runtime cache and shape utils

**Relations are computed once per mount.** In `Tldraw.tsx:756-782`, `allRelations = useMemo(() => { const relations = getDiscourseRelations(); discourseContext.relations = …by label… }, [])`, and `allRelationIds` / `allRelationNames` derive from it. Nodes work the same way (lines 783-790).

**Shape utils, bindings and tools are keyed by relation id:**
- `createAllRelationShapeUtils(allRelationIds)` (`DiscourseRelationUtil.tsx:617`) creates one class per id with `static type = id`, plus a fallback `"discourse-relation"` util whose `handleCreateRelationsInRoam` does nothing (lines 1224-1230; prop `relationTypeId` is unused).
- `createAllRelationBindings(allRelationIds)` does the same per id.
- The utils are wired through `useCanvasStoreAdapterArgs.ts:61-196` into `createTLStore({shapeUtils, bindingUtils})` (`useRoamStore.ts:92`) and `<TldrawEditor shapeUtils bindingUtils>` (`Tldraw.tsx:1342-1344`).
- Relation tools are keyed by **label** (`createAllRelationShapeTools(allRelationNames)`), as are the UI overrides and the tool panel.
- Migrations take `allRelationIds` (`discourseRelationMigrations.ts`).
- The Cloudflare room schema is built from the client's `shapeType` / `bindingType` URL params and merged (`apps/tldraw-sync-worker/worker/TldrawDurableObject.ts:19-157`), so reconnecting with new types extends it.

**Consequence.** A relation created mid-session is not a registered type. Also, `handleCreateRelationsInRoam` switches to `matchingRelation.id` (line 694) even when you create the arrow with a same-label sibling id, and that will fail for a new id.

**Refresh options:**
- **(a)** After the write, set `discourseContext.relations` again from `getDiscourseRelations()` (after `refreshConfigTree()`) so the menu updates. Then force a remount of the canvas (key or state on `TldrawCanvasShared`) so utils, bindings, tools and the store are rebuilt. The local store reloads from page props. Remounting loses undo history and selection.
- **(b)** For "Add existing" only: create the arrow with an existing same-label relation id, and guard the type switch in `handleCreateRelationsInRoam` so it skips when no util exists. Persist with the new record's id through `createReifiedRelation`. On reload the arrow keeps the old type, which `checkConnectionTypeAcrossLabel` tolerates.
- "Create new" (a new label) has no existing util, so it needs a remount or the fallback-type route with custom persistence.

## 5. Dialogs, toasts, color pickers

**Canvas toasts:** `dispatchToastEvent({id, title, description?, severity})` (`src/components/canvas/ToastListener.tsx`; a document CustomEvent picked up by tldraw `useToasts` in the `OnTheCanvas` slot). I've sent the full report to the agent that launched me. Two things will shape how you build this in Roam.

- **Roam has no separate relation type.** Each relation is one record: label, complement, source node type and destination node type, plus optional query conditions ("If" triples). No color is stored; color is worked out from the label.
  - So "add existing" means creating a new record that copies the label and complement onto the new pair. The closest existing code is `createRelationSchema` in `src/utils/createRelationSchema.ts`, used by the cross-app import.
  - A "Create new" dialog that saves a color would need a new schema field.
- **A relation created mid-session can't be drawn yet.** Each relation id becomes its own tldraw shape and binding type, built once when the canvas mounts. Creating an arrow with a new id fails until the canvas remounts.
  - "Create new" (a new label) therefore needs a canvas remount or custom handling.
  - For "add existing", a same-label relation's shape can be reused, with a small guard in the save code.

Other points you'll need:
- **Two stores:** the old settings blocks are what's read today on main, because the "Use new settings store" flag is off by default. The settings panel and the import both write to both stores, so the new code must too.
- **Required conditions:** a record with no query conditions only works when the "stored relations" setting is on. It defaults on for installs after 2026-03-01. With it off, the record is invisible to the canvas unless you add conditions.
- **Refreshing:** after creating a record, call `refreshConfigTree()` and rebuild the canvas's relation list. The menu itself also needs a trigger to recompute, since it only computes its options once.
- **Menu closing:** the menu's outside-click and Escape listeners will close it when a sub-menu or dialog opens, so they need a guard.
- **Styling:** the extension relies on Roam's global Tailwind, which has no arbitrary-value classes. Classes like `max-h-[240px]` in the current menu likely don't apply, so use Blueprint components.
- **Tests:** unit tests only pick up files under `src/utils/__tests__`, so new logic should live in `src/utils` to be testable.

The report also covers the drag-and-drop gate and its toast, how picking a type creates and saves the arrow, the toast and dialog patterns, the existing color input, and the AGENTS.md rules, all with file and line references.
